chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ghurāb, who said:

Al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad said: “Whoever is alone with a sin, then watches Allah, exalted is His mention, concerning it, and feels ashamed before the recording angels, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will forgive all his sins, even if they are like the sins of the two weighty beings.”

key_terms.الْحَفَظَةِ: the recording angels who preserve a person’s deeds
key_terms.بِذَنْبٍ: a sin or act of disobedience
key_terms.ذُنُوبِ الثَّقَلَيْنِ: the sins of humankind and jinn together
key_terms.ذِكْرُهُ: His mention; an expression of glorification for Allah
key_terms.فَرَاقَبَ اللَّهَ: he remained conscious of Allah and watched himself before Him

ai.seo_question: Can Allah forgive private sins if a person feels ashamed and fears Him afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that private sin does not place a person beyond Allah’s forgiveness if it is followed by God-consciousness and shame before the heavenly recorders. It emphasizes muraqabah, haya', and the vastness of divine forgiveness, even for very great sins.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5895 - Al-Husayn ibn Yazid narrated from Ali ibn Ghurab who said:

Abu Abdullah (as), said: "Whoever commits a sin in private and then fears Allah (swt), exalted be His (swt) mention, regarding it, and feels ashamed before the recording angels; Allah (swt), the Majestic, will forgive all his sins, even if they are as numerous as the sins of the two weighty beings (humankind and jinn)."
